title: The dancer and the watcher
hookLine: Samkhya's dancer: nature performs, the self watches, and yoga's 'just watch your thoughts' starts here
carry: the mind is nature's dance; the self is the watcher
tomorrow: The goddess says: I am Brahman
last: ALL OF THIS IS MINE, AND THERE IS MORE.

lines: A DANCER, A STAGE, AN AUDIENCE.
cards: A dancer steps onto a stage. She moves, turns, tells a whole story with her hands and eyes. The audience watches.
At some point the dance is complete: everything she came to show has been shown. So she stops, and walks off.
That small scene is a picture from Samkhya, one of the philosophical schools of India, in a short book of verses called the Samkhya Karika. It's a cool, careful map of the world, not a hymn.
But its picture of nature as a performer belongs right next to Shakti.

teach.b: Samkhya names two principles. Purusha: pure awareness, the one who watches. Prakriti: nature, everything that moves and changes.
Here's the surprise: in Samkhya, the mind sits on nature's side. Thoughts, moods, memory, even the sense of I: all of it is prakriti, part of the dance. The self is the one watching.
The verse, in paraphrase: as a dancer stops after showing herself to the audience, so prakriti stops after showing herself to purusha. Why does she dance at all?
The Samkhya Karika says nature works for the watcher's sake, so it can see, and be free.
And the tenderest line: nothing is more modest than prakriti. Once she knows she's been seen, she does not show herself again.

teach.h: YOU ARE NOT THE STORM OF THOUGHTS.
teach.b: So here is the teaching: you are not the storm of thoughts; you are the one who sees it. Many teachers read Samkhya's freedom just this way: the watcher no longer mistaking the dance for itself.
The Yoga Sutras build on this map.

teach.h: THEN THE SEER RESTS IN ITSELF.
teach.b: Yoga, they say, is the stilling of the mind's turnings, and then the seer rests in its own nature. So when a yoga class says just watch your thoughts, that isn't a wellness slogan. It's a Hindu map of the self.
Today: the night before something big, the mind stages every way it could go wrong.
Samkhya doesn't tell you to fight the show. It tells you who's in the audience. One difference to keep: in Samkhya, prakriti isn't a goddess.
Goddess traditions take the same picture and say the dancer is Shakti herself. That's tomorrow.

how: The Samkhya Karika is studied in courses on Indian philosophy and in yoga schools, where its two principles, purusha and prakriti, are used to explain the Yoga Sutras.

games.q: what does “shakti as a philosophy” mean?
o: a stage art that tells the stories of the gods
a rule that the body must stay perfectly still
nature as a dancer, moving so the watcher goes free

p: the self: pure awareness, the watcher
stops once she has been seen

s: in Samkhya, your thoughts belong to the self
thoughts, moods, even the sense of I are prakriti, nature's side. the self, purusha, only watches.
the Yoga Sutras build on Samkhya's watcher and watched
yoga stills the mind's turnings, and then the seer rests in its own nature.
Samkhya worships prakriti as a goddess
in Samkhya prakriti is a principle in a system, not a goddess. goddess traditions read the picture differently.

games.q: the night before a big test, your mind replays every way it could go wrong. by Samkhya's map, what's going on?
o: that's you: you are your worries.
that's prakriti dancing; you're the one watching it.
that's purusha moving; awareness is restless by nature.
games.why: in Samkhya the mind belongs to nature's dance. the self, purusha, only watches, and freedom starts when it stops mistaking the show for itself.

practice: Sit still and let yourself be the audience: thoughts, sounds and feelings will come onstage, a plan, a passing car, an itch.
Don't chase any of them off; watch each one the way you'd watch a dancer, with interest, until it has finished showing itself and leaves.
If you pray, you can rest in the name you use for the divine; if you don't, rest in the watching.

wordCard.voice: Shakti as a philosophy. In Samkhya, prakriti dances for purusha, the watcher, and when she has been fully seen, she stops.

orig.note: Sanskrit: purusha, in Samkhya the pure awareness that watches nature's dance.
